items.title: Lillian De Pass Interview, 1960-06-20
items.q: The interviewee discusses Octave Boye in the third person, referring to him as 'he' and 'your daddy' (the interviewer's father) sent him to jobs. There is no indication that Lillian De Pass personally knew, met, or collaborated with Octave Boye; she is narrating the history of the interviewer's fami

ctx.x: No, he was from around here. Not around here, but around... Around... Around... Prairie Street. Around... Around Caloret, Laperouse. And then when he was small and his mother was living and all, they lived back Olyan and... Olyan and... Olyan and... Olyan and... Russia Blade. Olyan and Russia Blade, yeah. They lived around there. But he'd come up right in the... He'd come up after that, when the time he started the band and all that, right there in the Tramie. You know, right in the Tramie. That was the best part…

Octave Boye. Well, he played for a couple of years, you know. He didn't keep it up. But most of the way he went to play, your daddy would recommend him to go... You know, when people would ask. Well, the most of the way he went through his life playing music, and everybody addressed him always as the past. You know, your daddy would send him, they knew he was the brother, and he'd never take it and explain him. Just Uncle Rudolph would after. Good many years, well, he'd put out his name, Boye, you see.
